title: Retain all-fixed-sector nonnegativity under explicit local errors
statement: For0<g<=.4,|delta|<=.1,|epsilon|<=.1,the perturbed one-body ladder is nonnegative and its second-quantized hard-core compression remains nonnegative in every fixed particle sector. The first-rung Schur matrix is[[2.5+sqrt(6),epsilon],[epsilon,.5]]>=.4 I;the memory Schur complement is>=2.9-.32/.4=2.1.

requires: Same bounded number-conserving ladder,relative memory and antisymmetric first-rung frequency controls
All remaining rail tails retained at the lower zero-energy endpoint
provides: Explicit local-control stability box for the full one-body form
Nonnegativity survives second quantization and compression in each fixed excitation sector
assumptions: The lower bath band is gapless at zero;the endpoint inverse quadratic form is finite even though the full tail has no bounded inverse there
The stability box is not a pole-radius box
No strictly positive global gap or arbitrary occupancy/storage-capacity theorem is inferred
costs: Ideal Hamiltonian inequalities;no actuator/noise implementation acquired
All tail elimination,endpoint coupling norm and memory bounds are retained
contract.units: Hamiltonian quadratic-form nonnegativity in each fixed particle sector
contract.obstruction: Stability alone supplies no lifetime,gate performance or uniform detuning continuation radius.

evidence.quote: The limits here are delta to zero at fixed g, then g to zero for the coefficient.
evidence.range_scope: Local continued pole at fixed sufficiently small nonzero g, ordered detuning coefficient, coherent first-rung compensation and explicit nonnegativity box; no finite-error gate certificate.

evidence.quote: P17 — ACCEPT at its declared mathematical scope

Actual warm follow-up accepts joint-parameter local continuation, coherent response and stability at their declared scopes; P84 exact rational positivity reconstruction.

body: The proved bound uses a form Schur complement at the gapless threshold. Replacing it with a claimed bounded inverse of the complete tail would be incorrect.
